# Finance Business Glossary

**Source:** [Confluence: KCD / Finance Business Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8486916)

## Identity
- **Type:** Confluence page
- **Purpose (1 sentence):** This page provides a plain-language glossary of key financial metrics and concepts to establish a shared terminology for analysts, product, and reporting teams across finance reporting.
- **Status (if stated):** (none)

## Topics and Entities
Net Interest Margin, NIM, Credit Risk Score, Customer Lifetime Value, CLV, LTV, Finance Data & Analytics, KCD, analysts, product, reporting teams, net interest income, average interest-earning assets, earnings, treasury reviews, KYC risk rating, Marketing decks, customer LTV, financial-crime risk, default risk, balance sheet, lending decisions, loan pricing, acquisition and retention investment

## Key Claims and Facts
- The document provides a plain-language glossary of key financial metrics and concepts.
- The glossary's purpose is to ensure analysts, product, and reporting teams use the same meaning for the same terms.
- The definitions in this glossary exclude system or field details.
- Net Interest Margin (NIM) is a profitability metric.
- NIM is calculated as net interest income divided by average interest-earning assets.
- NIM expresses how much margin the balance sheet produces per dollar of earning assets.
- NIM is reported in earnings and treasury reviews.
- NIM moves with the interest-rate environment.
- Credit Risk Score is a quantified estimate of how likely a borrower is to default.
- Credit Risk Score is built from repayment history, current exposure, and income or leverage.
- Credit Risk Score drives lending decisions and loan pricing.
- Lower Credit Risk Scores indicate higher default risk.
- Credit Risk Score is used both at origination and for ongoing portfolio monitoring.
- Credit Risk Score is distinct from a customer's KYC risk rating.
- A customer's KYC risk rating measures financial-crime risk, not default risk.
- Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) is the total net profit expected from a customer over their entire relationship.
- CLV is projected revenue from the customer minus the cost to serve and retain them, across their expected lifetime.
- CLV is used to decide how much can be justified spending to acquire and keep a customer.
- A high-CLV segment warrants more acquisition and retention investment than a low-CLV one.
- Marketing decks often use the terms "customer LTV" or "LTV" for Customer Lifetime Value.
- Finance reporting uses the term "CLV" for this metric.
- "customer LTV," "LTV," and "CLV" refer to the same metric (the lifetime value of a customer) and should not be treated as two different measures.

(none)

# Network Engineering Glossary

**Source:** [Confluence: KCD / Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985)

## Identity
- **Type:** Confluence page
- **Purpose (1 sentence):** This document defines key telecom and mobile network engineering terms used daily by the platform and network teams as a shared reference.

## Topics and Entities
APN, Access Point Name, IMSI, International Mobile Subscriber Identity, QoS, Quality of Service, VoLTE, Voice over LTE, Mobile Core Engineering, platform and network teams, packet data network, core, gateway, public-internet APN, internal IMS APN, voice signaling, data session, data profile, services, policies, subscriber, SIM, roaming, operator's network, traffic, latency, packet loss, throughput, classes, treatment, Real-time services, best-effort data, LTE data network, IMS, legacy circuit-switched voice path, QoS class, QoS Policy, SIM identity, Voice-over-LTE, IMS voice, New network and platform engineers, dedicated design docs

## Key Claims and Facts
- The document is a shared reference for mobile-network terms.
- The glossary owner is Mobile Core Engineering.
- The glossary audience is New network and platform engineers.
- Deeper treatment for terms lives in dedicated design docs.
- APN (Access Point Name) is the identifier a device presents to the network to say which packet data network it wants to reach.
- APN tells the core which gateway to route a data session through.
- Examples of APNs include a public-internet APN and an internal IMS APN for voice signaling.
- The APN is part of the device's data profile.
- The APN is applied when a data session is established.
- Different APNs can map to different services and policies.
- IMSI (International Mobile Subscriber Identity) is the globally unique identity of a subscriber.
- IMSI is provisioned onto the SIM.
- The network uses IMSI to recognize and authenticate a subscriber.
- IMSI is the key reference used when subscribers connect, at home or via roaming, on another operator's network.
- QoS (Quality of Service) is the set of mechanisms that prioritize traffic and hold it to performance targets.
- Performance targets for QoS include latency, packet loss, and throughput.
- Traffic is sorted into classes for QoS.
- Each QoS class is given a treatment appropriate to its needs.
- Real-time services need stricter QoS than best-effort data.
- VoLTE (Voice over LTE) carries voice calls as packets over the LTE data network (via IMS).
- VoLTE carries voice calls over the LTE data network rather than over the legacy circuit-switched voice path.
- VoLTE depends on a high-priority QoS class to keep calls clear.
- The specific QoS targets for VoLTE are defined in the QoS Policy.
- "SIM identity" is sometimes used loosely to mean the IMSI.
- "IMSI" is preferred over "SIM identity" in engineering docs.
- Voice-over-LTE, VoLTE, and "IMS voice" all refer to the same service.

(none)

# Billing & Charging System Overview

**Source:** [Confluence: KCD / Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)

## Identity
- **Type:** Confluence page
- **Purpose (1 sentence):** This document outlines the high-level mechanisms of the billing platform, explaining the lifecycle of usage events from rating to invoicing.

## Topics and Entities
Rating, Billing, Billing cycle, Prepaid, Postpaid, QoS, Quality of Service, Billing Platform Engineering, usage events, money, price plan, charge, invoice, customer base, invoicing load, month, plan type, balance, plan allowances, data plans, data allowance, QoS treatment, full-speed data, threshold, subscriber, traffic, lower-priority QoS class, throttling, charging system, policy function, discrepancies, review

## Key Claims and Facts
*   The document provides a high-level conceptual overview of the billing platform, explaining how usage becomes a bill, without schema detail.
*   The system turns raw usage events into money in two conceptual stages: rating and billing.
*   Rating applies the customer's price plan to each usage event to compute a charge.
*   Billing accumulates rated charges over the customer's billing cycle and produces an invoice at the cycle close.
*   The billing cycle is the recurring period over which usage is aggregated.
*   Each subscriber belongs to a billing cycle.
*   Cycle boundaries are staggered across the customer base.
*   Staggering cycle boundaries spreads invoicing load through the month.
*   For Postpaid plans, usage is rated and accumulated across the cycle, then invoiced at the end.
*   Postpaid customers pay in arrears.
*   For Prepaid plans, charges are decremented from a balance in real time as usage occurs.
*   For Prepaid plans, the "cycle" is mainly a window for plan allowances rather than an invoice period.
*   Charging and QoS (Quality of Service) intersect for data plans.
*   Some plans tie a data allowance to a QoS treatment.
*   An example QoS treatment is full-speed data up to a threshold, after which the subscriber's traffic is moved to a lower-priority QoS class (commonly experienced as "throttling") rather than being cut off.
*   The charging system signals the policy function when a threshold is crossed.
*   The policy function applies the appropriate QoS class for the remainder of the cycle.
*   At cycle close, rated charges are reconciled against the invoice total before issuance.
*   Discrepancies are held for review rather than billed.
*   The owner of this overview is Billing Platform Engineering.
*   The audience for this overview is Engineers and analysts working with charging and invoicing.

# Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview

**Source:** [Confluence: KCD / Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)

## Identity
- **Type:** Confluence page
- **Purpose (1 sentence):** This overview explains how IMSI and APN work together as critical metadata for subscriber identity and network session access control for new analysts and partners.

## Topics and Entities
IMSI, International Mobile Subscriber Identity, APN, Access Point Name, SIM, VoLTE, Mobile Core Engineering, KCD, packet data network, IMS APN, subscriber, device, network, home network, visited network, data session, subscriber records, session logs, identity, access

## Key Claims and Facts
- The document provides a meaning-first overview of how subscriber identity and data access fit together.
- The overview is deliberately conceptual, with no field or schema detail.
- IMSI (International Mobile Subscriber Identity) is at the center of a mobile subscriber.
- IMSI is the globally unique identifier of the subscriber.
- IMSI is held on the SIM.
- The network authenticates the IMSI when a device tries to connect.
- The IMSI acts as the subscriber's passport, proving identity to the home network and allowing a visited network to find and check with their home network.
- Almost everything the network does for a subscriber begins by resolving their IMSI.
- APN (Access Point Name) decides what a subscriber can reach on the network.
- The APN names the packet data network a session should connect to.
- The APN selects the gateway and the policies that apply for a session.
- One subscriber may have several APNs.
- Examples of APNs include a general internet APN and a separate IMS APN that carries voice signaling for VoLTE.
- Choosing the right APN makes a data session land on the right service with the right treatment.
- The IMSI answers "who is this subscriber?".
- The APN answers "what network/service is this session for?".
- A subscriber must be authenticated by IMSI before any session is established.
- Each session then uses an APN to reach its destination.
- Misconfiguring the IMSI means the device cannot attach at all.
- Misconfiguring the APN means the device attaches but cannot reach the intended service.
- In subscriber records or session logs, the IMSI is expected to be the join key for "which subscriber".
- In subscriber records or session logs, the APN is expected to indicate "which service/network" a session used.
- Keeping the distinction clear avoids conflating identity with access.

- [Confluence: KCD / Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)

# Roaming Partner Agreement — Summary

**Source:** [Confluence: KCD / Roaming Partner Agreement — Summary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519701)

## Identity
- **Type:** Confluence page
- **Purpose (1 sentence):** This document clarifies the core mechanism and identifiers, particularly the IMSI, used to authenticate and route mobile subscribers roaming on partner networks.

## Topics and Entities
Roaming Partner Agreement, IMSI, International Mobile Subscriber Identity, VoLTE, Roaming & Interconnect Business, KCD, Roaming managers, settlement analysts, subscriber, operator, network, visited network, home operator, wholesale rates, Voice, Data, Messaging, inter-operator charges, settlement rates, Coverage, service scope, Fraud, Usage controls, billing period

## Key Claims and Facts
- A roaming agreement is a bilateral arrangement with another operator.
- Roaming agreements allow each party's subscribers to use the other's network when outside home coverage.
- When one of our subscribers travels into a partner's footprint, the partner's network serves them as a "visited network."
- Without a roaming agreement, a subscriber abroad would simply have no service.
- Roaming relies on the IMSI (International Mobile Subscriber Identity) to differentiate home subscribers from the visited network's own.
- When a device attaches to a visited network, that network reads the IMSI.
- The visited network identifies the home operator from the IMSI.
- The visited network signals home to authenticate the subscriber and authorize service.
- Every clause about which subscribers are covered ultimately keys off the IMSI ranges assigned to each party.
- Roaming agreements fix the wholesale rates each operator charges the other for voice, data, and messaging consumed by visiting subscribers.
- Inter-operator charges are reconciled and settled periodically.
- Roaming agreements specify which services (e.g., data, VoLTE) are supported for roamers.
- Roaming agreements specify any technical preconditions for services.
- Roaming agreements include provisions for near-real-time usage exchange to catch abnormal roaming usage early.
- Roaming managers monitor partner reachability and the quality roamers receive.
- Settlement analysts reconcile wholesale charges against the agreed rates each billing period.
- The legal text of a roaming agreement governs.
- This document serves as an orientation to roaming agreements.

--- BATCH SUMMARY 1 ---
# Master Scope: Metadata Enrichment

This document aggregates, categorizes, and structures key operational and technical metadata definitions across corporate domain boundaries (Finance, Network Engineering, Billing Systems, and Telecom Operations). By establishing a structured, meaning-first reference, this knowledge base aligns technical schemas, operational policies, and analytics reporting.

---

## 1. Subscriber Identity and Network Session Metadata
*This sub-topic governs how core subscriber identities and access identifiers function as critical metadata keys for network routing, service access control, and data engineering joins.*

### International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI)
*   **Definition & Function:** IMSI is the globally unique identifier of a subscriber, provisioned onto the physical SIM card. It acts as the subscriber’s passport, proving identity to the home network and allowing a visited network to locate and verify the home operator [[Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)].
*   **System Interactions:** 
    *   The network must authenticate the IMSI before any session can be established. Misconfiguration of the IMSI prevents a device from attaching to the network at all [[Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)].
    *   It is the preferred term in engineering documentation over the loose synonym "SIM identity" [[Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985)].
*   **Data Analysis & Logs:** In subscriber records and network session logs, the IMSI is the primary join key used to resolve "which subscriber" initiated an action [[Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)].
*   **Roaming Applications:** Roaming relies on IMSI ranges to differentiate home subscribers from a visited network’s native users. Visited networks read the IMSI to identify the home operator, signaling back to authenticate the subscriber and authorize service under bilateral wholesale terms [[Roaming Partner Agreement — Summary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519701)].

### Access Point Name (APN)
*   **Definition & Function:** APN is the network identifier presented by a device during session establishment to specify which packet data network (PDN) it intends to reach [[Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985)]. It dictates the specific gateway, policies, and services applied to a given data session [[Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)].
*   **Key Distinction (Identity vs. Access):** While IMSI answers "who is this subscriber?", APN answers "what network/service is this session for?" [[Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)]. 
*   **Configuration Impact:** Misconfigured APN metadata allows a device to attach to the network but blocks it from reaching its target services. A subscriber may map to multiple APNs concurrently (e.g., a "public-internet APN" for general web traffic and an internal "IMS APN" dedicated to voice signaling) [[Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985), [Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)].
*   **Data Analysis:** In session logs, the APN is the core metadata field indicating "which service/network" was utilized [[Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)].

---

## 2. Policy, Network performance, and Voice Quality Metadata
*This sub-topic details the operational rules and quality configurations that govern live data traffic and voice session delivery.*

### Quality of Service (QoS)
*   **Operational Control:** QoS represents the set of mechanisms used to prioritize network traffic and hold sessions to specific performance targets (such as latency, packet loss, and throughput) [[Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985)].
*   **Class Differentiation:** Traffic is mapped to distinct QoS classes to receive appropriate priority treatments. Real-time services (e.g., voice) demand stricter QoS envelopes compared to standard "best-effort" data traffic [[Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985)].

### Voice over LTE (VoLTE) / IMS Voice
*   **Technology & Routing:** VoLTE (synonymous with "Voice-over-LTE" and "IMS voice") routes voice calls as packetized data over the LTE network via the IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) core rather than using legacy circuit-switched voice paths [[Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985)].
*   **Quality Dependency:** VoLTE calls rely on a dedicated, high-priority QoS class to guarantee call clarity. These target thresholds are formalized in the system's QoS Policy [[Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985)]. High-priority voice signaling is carried across a distinct IMS APN [[Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)].

---

## 3. Revenue Lifecycle and Billing Metadata
*This sub-topic defines the mechanics of converting real-time subscriber activity into financial statements, including rating, cycle schedules, and policy triggers.*

### Rating and Billing States
*   **Rating State:** This conceptual phase maps a customer’s assigned price plan to raw, incoming network usage events to compute a monetary charge [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].
*   **Billing State:** This phase aggregates rated charges over a predefined, recurring "billing cycle" and outputs a clean, reconciled invoice at cycle close [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].
*   **Invoicing Controls:**
    *   **Staggering:** To balance system load throughout the month, billing cycle boundaries are staggered across the customer base [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].
    *   **Reconciliation:** Prior to issuance, rated charges are reconciled against the final invoice total. Any detected discrepancies are put on hold for manual review instead of being processed [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].

### Prepaid vs. Postpaid Account Mechanics
*   **Postpaid Accounts:** Customers pay in arrears; usage metrics are accumulated throughout the active billing cycle and invoiced at its conclusion [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].
*   **Prepaid Accounts:** Balances are decremented in real time as usage occurs. For prepaid models, the "cycle" does not represent an invoice period, but rather an active window for resetting plan allowances [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].

### Charging-to-QoS Policy Feedback Loops
*   **Throttling Loops:** In certain data plans, physical data allowances are tied directly to QoS classifications. When a prepaid or postpaid subscriber crosses a specific usage threshold, the charging system signals the policy function [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].
*   **Execution:** Rather than cutting off the connection entirely, the policy engine downgrades the subscriber's session to a lower-priority QoS class (commonly called "throttling") for the remaining duration of the billing cycle [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].

---

## 4. Finance Business Glossary and Analytics Metrics
*This sub-topic establishes corporate definitions for key financial indicators to align analytics, treasury, marketing, and risk reporting.*

### Net Interest Margin (NIM)
*   **Definition & Formula:** NIM is a core profitability metric that measures the net yield generated by a firm's balance sheet per dollar of earning assets. It is calculated as:
    $$\text{NIM} = \frac{\text{Net Interest Income}}{\text{Average Interest-Earning Assets}}$$
*   **Reporting:** NIM fluctuates with changes in the interest-rate environment and is primarily reported in corporate earnings and treasury reviews [[Finance Business Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8486916)].

### Credit Risk Score
*   **Definition & Purpose:** A numerical projection of the probability that a borrower will default on a credit obligation. It is constructed using historical repayment patterns, outstanding exposures, and income or leverage profiles [[Finance Business Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8486916)].
*   **Applications:** It drives lending decisions, loan pricing, and ongoing portfolio risk monitoring. Lower risk scores flag higher probabilities of default [[Finance Business Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8486916)].
*   **Distinction from KYC Risk Rating:** Credit Risk Score must not be conflated with Know Your Customer (KYC) risk ratings; the former measures default probability, whereas the KYC rating evaluates financial-crime and compliance risk [[Finance Business Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8486916)].

### Customer Lifetime Value (CLV / LTV)
*   **Definition & Formula:** CLV represents the total net profit expected from a customer over the entire duration of their relationship. It is calculated as:
    $$\text{CLV} = \text{Projected Customer Revenue} - (\text{Cost to Serve} + \text{Cost to Retain})$$
*   **Business Application:** It justifies customer acquisition and retention budgets. Segmenting users by CLV ensures high-value cohorts receive proportionally higher investments [[Finance Business Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8486916)].
*   **Semantic Alignment:** Marketing materials frequently use "customer LTV" or "LTV", whereas official Finance reporting standardized on "CLV". Analytics pipelines must map these synonyms to the same single metric to prevent dual-definition errors [[Finance Business Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8486916)].

# International Mobile Subscriber Identity Overview

The International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) is a globally unique identifier provisioned onto the physical SIM card, serving as the subscriber's digital passport. It proves identity to the home network and allows a visited network to locate and verify the home operator. The IMSI is crucial for network authentication, roaming, and data logging.

## Key Features and Role

*   **Globally Unique Identifier**: IMSI is the unique identity of a subscriber, stored on the physical SIM card.
*   **Network Authentication**: Before any session can be established, the network must authenticate the IMSI. Misconfiguration of the IMSI prevents a device from attaching to the network at all.
*   **Roaming**: In roaming scenarios, networks use IMSI ranges to differentiate home subscribers from those of a visited network. The visited network reads the IMSI to identify the home operator, signaling back to authenticate the subscriber and authorize service under bilateral wholesale terms.
*   **Data Analysis and Metadata Enrichment**: In subscriber records and network session logs, the IMSI acts as the primary join key. It is used to resolve "which subscriber" initiated an action, providing a fundamental piece of metadata for understanding user activity.
*   **Terminology**: While "SIM identity" is a loose synonym, "International Mobile Subscriber Identity" or "IMSI" is the preferred term in engineering documentation.
*   **Distinction from APN**: The IMSI answers the question "who is this subscriber?", distinguishing it from the Access Point Name (APN), which answers "what network/service is this session for?".

# Access Point Name Overview

An Access Point Name (APN) serves as a network identifier that a device presents during session establishment. It specifies the packet data network (PDN) the device intends to reach, dictating the specific gateway, policies, and services to be applied to a given data session.

## Definition and Function

The APN is fundamental for session establishment, acting as a crucial piece of metadata that defines the characteristics of a data connection. While an International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) identifies "who is this subscriber?", the APN clarifies "what network/service is this session for?" [[Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)]. It directs traffic to the correct packet data network and ensures appropriate service parameters are applied [[Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985)].

## Role as a Metadata Field

In data analysis, particularly within session logs, the APN is a core metadata field that indicates which service or network was utilized for a specific session [[Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)]. Its accurate configuration is vital; misconfigured APN metadata can allow a device to connect to the network but prevent it from accessing its intended services [[Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985)].

## Configuration and Usage Scenarios

A single subscriber may utilize multiple APNs concurrently to access different services. For instance, a "public-internet APN" might handle general web traffic, while a dedicated "IMS APN" manages internal voice signaling [[Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985), [Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)].

## Example: VoLTE and IMS APN

For Voice over LTE (VoLTE) calls, which route voice as packetized data over the LTE network via the IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) core, a distinct IMS APN is used. This dedicated APN carries high-priority voice signaling and is crucial for ensuring the call clarity dependent on a dedicated, high-priority Quality of Service (QoS) class defined in the system's QoS Policy [[Network Engineering Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8617985), [Telecom Systems & Terminology Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8552489)].

# Quality of Service Overview

Quality of Service (QoS) refers to the mechanisms used to prioritize network traffic and manage packet delivery to meet specific performance targets, such as latency, packet loss, and throughput. It represents an operational control that holds network sessions to these defined performance standards.

## Key Features and Operational Control

QoS facilitates the prioritization of network traffic through **class differentiation**. Traffic is mapped to distinct QoS classes, each receiving appropriate priority treatments. For instance, real-time services like voice communication demand stricter QoS envelopes compared to standard "best-effort" data traffic, ensuring their critical performance requirements are met.

## Applications and Dependencies

### Voice over LTE (VoLTE)
VoLTE, also known as "Voice-over-LTE" or "IMS voice," routes voice calls as packetized data over the LTE network using the IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) core. VoLTE calls critically rely on a dedicated, high-priority QoS class to guarantee call clarity. The target thresholds for this are formalized within the system's QoS Policy. High-priority voice signaling for VoLTE is carried across a distinct IMS Access Point Name (APN).

### Charging-to-QoS Policy Feedback Loops
QoS classifications are integrated into certain data plans, directly linking physical data allowances to network prioritization. In scenarios where a prepaid or postpaid subscriber exceeds a specific usage threshold, the charging system signals the policy function. Instead of completely cutting off the connection, the policy engine then downgrades the subscriber's session to a lower-priority QoS class, a process commonly referred to as "throttling," for the remainder of the billing cycle.

# Rating and Billing States Overview

Rating and Billing States describe the operational stages involved in mapping customer price plans to network usage events and subsequently aggregating these into validated, reconciled invoices throughout active billing cycles. This process covers two main phases: Rating State and Billing State.

## Key Concepts

### Rating State
The **Rating State** is a conceptual phase focused on calculating a monetary charge. During this phase, a customer’s assigned price plan is applied to raw, incoming network usage events to determine the cost.

### Billing State
The **Billing State** phase involves aggregating the charges computed during the Rating State. These rated charges are collected over a predefined, recurring "billing cycle" to ultimately produce a clean, reconciled invoice at the close of each cycle.

## Invoicing Controls
Several controls are in place to manage the invoicing process within the Billing State:

*   **Staggering:** To distribute the system load evenly throughout the month, billing cycle boundaries are staggered across the customer base.
*   **Reconciliation:** Before invoices are issued, all rated charges undergo a reconciliation process against the final invoice total. Any discrepancies detected during this reconciliation are put on hold for manual review, preventing incorrect charges from being processed.

## Source References

This document aggregates, categorizes, and structures key operational and technical metadata definitions across corporate domain boundaries (Finance, Network Engineering, Billing Systems, and Telecom Operations). ## 1. Subscriber Identity and Network Session Metadata

## 4. Finance Business Glossary and Analytics Metrics

# Account Billing Mechanics Overview

Account Billing Mechanics define the logic governing real-time account updates and actions taken during a billing cycle, encompassing balance reductions, deferred payments, and Quality of Service (QoS) throttling loops. This entry, also referred to by aliases such as prepaid-accounts, postpaid-accounts, and charging-to-qos-policy-feedback-loops, describes the processes that convert subscriber activity into financial statements within the broader Revenue Lifecycle and Billing Metadata domain.

## Key Concepts

### Prepaid vs. Postpaid Account Mechanics
The system distinguishes between two primary account types:
*   **Postpaid Accounts:** Customers incur usage first and are billed in arrears. Usage metrics accumulate over an active billing cycle, leading to an invoice at the cycle's conclusion [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].
*   **Prepaid Accounts:** Balances are reduced in real time as usage occurs. For prepaid models, the "cycle" denotes an active window for resetting plan allowances rather than an invoice period [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].

### Rating and Billing States
The financial conversion of subscriber activity occurs in distinct conceptual phases:
*   **Rating State:** This phase maps a customer's assigned price plan (a form of metadata) to incoming network usage events to calculate a monetary charge [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].
*   **Billing State:** This phase aggregates the rated charges over a predefined, recurring "billing cycle" to produce a reconciled invoice at the end of the cycle [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].
    *   **Invoicing Controls:** To manage system load, billing cycle boundaries are staggered across the customer base. Prior to issuance, rated charges are reconciled against the final invoice total, with any discrepancies flagged for manual review [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)].

### Charging-to-QoS Policy Feedback Loops
This mechanism links usage-based charging with network quality of service:
*   **Throttling Loops:** For certain data plans, physical data allowances are directly tied to QoS classifications. When a subscriber, whether prepaid or postpaid, exceeds a specific usage threshold, the charging system signals the policy function [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681]].
*   **Execution:** Instead of terminating the connection, the policy engine downgrades the subscriber's session to a lower-priority QoS class, a process known as "throttling," for the remainder of the billing cycle [[Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681]]. This dynamic adjustment of QoS classification acts as a metadata update triggered by billing conditions.

## Source References
*   [Billing & Charging System Overview](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8519681)

# Net Interest Margin Overview

Net Interest Margin (NIM) is a core corporate profitability metric that measures the net yield generated by a firm's balance sheet per dollar of earning assets. It tracks the net yield generated by earning assets relative to their average value, providing insight into the efficiency of a financial institution's interest-earning activities.

## Definition and Calculation

NIM is calculated by dividing the Net Interest Income by the Average Interest-Earning Assets. This metric quantifies the net yield generated by a firm's balance sheet per dollar of earning assets.

The formula for Net Interest Margin is:

$$\text{NIM} = \frac{\text{Net Interest Income}}{\text{Average Interest-Earning Assets}}$$

## Reporting and Fluctuations

NIM is primarily reported in corporate earnings and treasury reviews. Its value is known to fluctuate significantly with changes in the prevailing interest-rate environment.

## Aliases

This metric is also commonly referred to as NIM.

# Credit Risk Score Overview

The Credit Risk Score is a financial projection that quantifies the probability of a borrower defaulting on a credit obligation. This metric is distinct from compliance-driven Know Your Customer (KYC) ratings, focusing purely on financial default risk.

## Definition and Purpose

The Credit Risk Score is a numerical projection that estimates the likelihood of a borrower failing to meet their credit obligations. It is derived from an analysis of historical repayment patterns, current outstanding exposures, and the borrower's income or leverage profiles.

## Applications

This score is a critical tool that informs lending decisions, helps in the accurate pricing of loans, and supports ongoing monitoring of portfolio risk. A lower Credit Risk Score indicates a higher probability of default.

## Distinction from KYC Risk Rating

It is important to differentiate the Credit Risk Score from the Know Your Customer (KYC) risk rating. While the Credit Risk Score assesses the probability of default, the KYC rating specifically evaluates risks related to financial crime and compliance.

# Customer Lifetime Value Overview

Customer Lifetime Value (CLV), also known as LTV or Customer LTV, is a key financial and analytical metric that quantifies the net long-term profit projected from a customer over the entire duration of their relationship with the business. It is a standard metric used in corporate and analytical applications to understand the financial worth of customers.

## Definition and Formula

CLV represents the total net profit expected from a customer throughout their engagement. It is calculated using the following formula:

$$\text{CLV} = \text{Projected Customer Revenue} - (\text{Cost to Serve} + \text{Cost to Retain})$$

## Business Application

This metric is crucial for justifying budgets related to customer acquisition and retention. By segmenting users based on their CLV, businesses can ensure that high-value customer cohorts receive proportionally higher investments, optimizing resource allocation [[Finance Business Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8486916)].

## Semantic Alignment

While marketing materials frequently use terms like "customer LTV" or "LTV," official Finance reporting has standardized on "CLV." Analytics pipelines are designed to map these synonyms to the single, consistent metric of Customer Lifetime Value to prevent potential dual-definition errors and ensure data accuracy [[Finance Business Glossary](https://atharva-test-izfs7ihz.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/KCD/pages/8486916)].
